text:
You need an online store homepage that lets you present products with description, price, and images, while also supporting cart checkout, online payment, delivery selection, bilingual ENG/LV content, and automatic invoice generation and email delivery.  

I can build this for you. I’m Tobias Reyne, and I have 7 years of experience working with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, full stack development, HTML, and CSS.

For a project like yours, I’d recommend a custom-built store rather than a platform with recurring subscription fees. That approach gives you more control over product management, checkout flow, invoice generation, and the ability to add or remove items later without depending on a rigid theme system.

A relevant project I completed was a booking platform for fitness studios built with Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Prisma, and Stripe. It was a white-label app where each studio had its own subdomain, timetable, and memberships. One result: 64 studios were onboarded in 6 months, and checkout conversion reached 71%. That experience is directly useful for your order flow, payment handling, and customer-facing account logic.

I also rebuilt a home goods storefront using Next.js, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, Sanity, and Vercel. The marketing team could edit content themselves, which is similar to your need for an easy-to-use product catalog that your team can manage later. One result from that work: largest contentful paint improved from 4.1s to 1.3s, and organic traffic increased by 38% in 3 months.

For your store, I would structure it around:
- a simple product management interface
- product pages with image, description, and price
- cart and checkout
- payment via Stripe
- delivery method selection
- invoice generation and email sending after order placement
- ENG/LV language support

I can’t give an exact cost without clarifying the final scope, but I can say this type of website is absolutely feasible. If you’d like, I can outline the recommended build approach and provide a more accurate estimate once we confirm the number of product types, invoice details, and delivery rules.
